lamagiadecantar.title: La Magia de Cantar
lamagiadecantar.subtitle: Vocal transformation platform in production for a real client: plan sales with a payment gateway, AI voice test, and a live database.

overview.label: Overview
overview.title: A live system, not a demo
overview.p1: La Magia de Cantar is the platform of TV vocal coach Yanetsis Alfonso. It is not a prototype: it is the production system the client uses to sell her classes, receive real payments, and manage her students. It is the only project in the portfolio with a backend, database, and payment gateway running live.
overview.p2: The frontend features a distinctive high-contrast design with golden accents, built to turn visitors into students: every section guides the user from discovering the method to purchasing a plan.

stack.label: Stack
stack.title: Technologies
stack.subtitle: Next.js (App Router + TypeScript), PostgreSQL (Supabase), Mercado Pago, Resend, Vercel.

problem.label: The problem
problem.title: Selling vocal training online, reliably
items: The client used to sell her classes through WhatsApp and manual transfers: no records, no automatic confirmation, and payment errors were common.
She needed a clear plan catalog (monthly, quarterly, yearly) and a checkout that charged online securely.
The process had to be reliable for the student and auditable for her: who paid, how much, and the real status of every order.

solution.label: The solution
solution.title: Catalog + checkout + automatic confirmation
items: The student picks a service and a plan from a catalog read from the database.
A checkout form captures student and payer data with validation and anti-spam protection.

architecture.label: Architecture
architecture.title: Payment module architecture
architecture.intro: This is how the systems connect: the browser talks to the Next.js server, which orchestrates the database (Supabase), the payment gateway (Mercado Pago), and transactional email (Resend). All money goes through the gateway; the server never trusts client data.
takeaways: The service and plan catalog is read from the database, not hard-coded.
Payment is charged through Mercado Pago using a token; the amount is always computed server-side.
Payment notifications arrive by webhook with a verified signature, are checked against the real payment status, and are logged in the database.
A cron expires abandoned orders and keeps the database clean.

process.label: Process
process.title: Payment process flow
process.intro: The full sequence, from choosing a plan to the email confirmation. Solid arrows are requests; dashed ones are responses and async notifications.
takeaways: The order is created first as 'draft' and only advances once the payment is approved.
Payment is confirmed twice: inline via the gateway response and later via webhook.
There is an anti-fraud reconciliation: the paid amount must match the official order total.
The confirmation email is sent only once (duplicate protection).

items.title: Mercado Pago checkout
items.description: Card, PSE and cash via Payment Brick; wallet preference for additional methods.

items.title: Plan catalog
items.description: Services with monthly, quarterly and yearly variants, read from the database.

items.title: AI voice test
items.description: Visitors record and receive a personalized verdict before buying.

items.title: Corporate quote
items.description: Multi-step form for companies and institutions requesting vocal training.

items.title: Webhooks & reconciliation
items.description: Signature verification, idempotency and amount validation against the order.

items.title: Transactional email
items.description: Purchase confirmation with service expectations via Resend.

value.label: Business value
value.title: Why it matters
items: The client sells online with secure, automated payments instead of manual transfers.
Every student has an order with a clear status: approved, pending or rejected.
The payment flow is protected: server-side amounts, validated webhooks and duplicate-safe emails.
It is a real system in production: proof the work goes all the way to deployment and collection.
